app.name: Trip Hotel Data
app.title: Trip Hotel Data · Trip.com hotel metadata
hero.lead: Descriptions, policies and nearby places for every hotel — synced automatically, stored right on your computer, with multilingual content ready to hand over whenever you need it.

setup.cityPlaceholder: Type a city (e.g. hk, bang) or #Vinfast, #GreenSM…
ids.pasteHelp:
One hotel per line, accepted forms:
• 1971156 — hotelId (4–12 digits)
• https://vn.trip.com/hotels/detail/?hotelId=1971156… — hotel page URL
• 2068285, 427787 — several IDs on one line, separated by comma / semicolon / tab
• ID: 427787 - Homeinn — extra text is fine, the first number is used
• Lines starting with # are comments and skipped
Duplicates are merged; unrecognised lines are listed after you click Check list.
ids.fileHelp:
No special format needed. The app scans every cell in the file and picks out hotelIds (4–12 digits) or Trip.com hotel URLs; header rows or extra columns are fine.

• .txt: one ID/URL per line
• .csv / .tsv: any column, separated by , ; or tab (UTF-8 or Excel)
• .xlsx: every sheet, every cell; numbers like 1.97E+06 are read correctly

After reading, the IDs are placed in the paste box on the left so you can review/edit them before syncing. Up to 5,000 hotels per run, file ≤ 25 MB.

backup.subtitle: Zips all data (source records, changes, session, export files) into one file. Back up before updating or uninstalling.

marks.title: "Exported" marks
marks.hint: The app remembers which hotels are already in an export file so the next export only includes new ones. Normally you don't need to touch this.
marks.resetConfirm:
Forget the "exported" marks?

After that ALL hotels count as "new" and the next "only new" export includes everything. Only use this to export from scratch.
marks.resetDone: Exported marks forgotten — every hotel is "new" now.
marks.allConfirm:
Mark ALL hotels as exported (without creating a file)?

After that only hotels synced again or newly synced count as "new".
